Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
26-year-old with previously well-controlled asthma now experiencing 2–3 days of wheeze, cough, and exertional dyspnea unrelieved by salbutamol.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Acute increase in shortness of breath, wheeze, and dry cough for 2–3 days; precipitated when running, now with brisk walking.  
• Associated symptoms: No sputum production; denies other features noted.  
• Asthma history: Diagnosed childhood (year not stated). Last attack 3–4 years ago; never hospitalized; no prior oral steroids. Last asthma nurse review ~2 years ago. Does not routinely record current peak flow; usual baseline ~380 L/min.  
• Medications:  
  – Salbutamol inhaler (blue), dose/route/frequency not documented (PRN).  
  – Clenil (beclomethasone) inhaler, previously 3 puffs twice daily.  
  – Cetraben cream, dose/frequency not documented.  
  – Hydrocortisone cream, dose/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: Seasonal hay fever; no known drug allergies.  
• Family history: Brother—asthma; sister—eczema.  
• Social / preventive: Not discussed.

Examination:
No examination performed (video consult only).  
Vitals: Not recorded.

Impression:
Likely mild asthma exacerbation.

Plan:
• Increase preventer: Clenil to 4 puffs twice daily.  
• Reliever: Salbutamol up to every 2–4 hours PRN; heavy use (>4-hourly) indicates worsening control.  
• Safety-net: If dyspnea worsens or salbutamol required very frequently, attend Emergency Department without delay.  
• Follow-up: Book face-to-face GP appointment within a few days for chest exam, peak-flow measurement, and full asthma review; possible need for oral steroids and/or antibiotics depending on findings.  
• No additional questions from patient.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Current peak-flow reading, vitals, full medication reconciliation (doses/routes), smoking status, immunizations.  
● Internal conflicts: Unclear preventer dose (patient stated “yes” to 3 puffs BID; doctor suggested increasing from 3 to 4 puffs BID).  
● Transcript quality: Occasional inaudible sections and truncations; overall main clinical content clear.
